commit.message:
Reuse d_tag slot for kind:30443 publishes to enable NIP-33 replacement (#835)

* fix(key_packages): reuse the kind:30443 d-tag across publishes

MDK's `create_key_package_for_event` generates a fresh random 32-byte hex
`d` tag every call ("Callers SHOULD store and reuse this value when
rotating the KeyPackage"). The whitenoise publish path was using
whatever MDK handed back each time, so consecutive publishes for the
same account landed in different NIP-33 addressable slots — relays
accumulated stale kind:30443 events instead of replacing them.

Persist the chosen d-tag in `published_key_packages` (the column already
existed) and look it up before each canonical publish. When a stored
d-tag is found, swap MDK's freshly-generated `Tag::identifier` in
`tags_30443` so the publish lands in the same slot and relays apply the
NIP-33 replacement. First publish for an account falls through and
records MDK's d-tag, which becomes the slot for all future publishes.

* fix(key_packages): fail the publish when loading the canonical d-tag errors

Per CodeRabbit feedback: silently falling back to MDK's fresh d-tag on a
DB read failure partially re-introduces the bug this PR fixes — one
transient failure would publish kind:30443 to a new NIP-33 slot and
leave the existing canonical event stale on relays. DB reads on the
per-account SQLite file are local and rare to fail; aborting lets the
scheduler retry on its next tick with consistent state.

* fix(key_packages): route scheduler republishes through canonical d-tag slot

Two follow-ups on the d-tag reuse fix:

P1: Scheduler-driven rotations bypassed the new canonical-slot logic.
`session.key_packages().publish()` only published kind:443 (legacy), so
the maintenance task's "no usable local key package" and
"all expired" rotations never refreshed the canonical kind:30443 event
at all — the d-tag slot would stay frozen on whatever the initial
account-setup publish wrote.

Refactor `KeyPackageOps::publish` and `create_and_publish` to publish
both kinds through a shared `publish_pair` helper that reuses the
persisted `d` tag and tracks every publish (canonical and legacy) in
the per-account DB. The global `Whitenoise::publish_key_package_pair_to_relays`
path stays for external-signer login flows, which still hand the signer
in explicitly.

P2: NIP-01 keeps the lowest-id event when two replaceable events share
a `created_at`, so reusing the d-tag alone does not guarantee
replacement under same-second rapid republishes — the new event might
lose the tiebreaker. Compute a strictly-monotonic `created_at` via
`monotonic_canonical_created_at`: read the prior maximum from
`published_key_packages.created_at` (the row insert timestamp, which is
always ≥ the previous event's `created_at`) and bump past it. This
relies on the existing column — no migration needed.

Plumb an optional `custom_created_at` through
`publish_key_package_with_signer` → `publish_event_builder_with_signer`
so the canonical leg can set its own timestamp. Legacy (kind:443) is
regular per NIP-01 and keeps `None` (default wall clock) since each
publish is independently addressable.

Test changes:
- New DB unit tests for `find_max_created_at`.
- New pure unit tests for `monotonic_canonical_created_at` covering
  empty / future-prior / past-prior / negative-prior cases.
- The integration-style replacement test now also asserts the relay
  surfaces exactly one canonical event for the slot after a second
  publish in the same second, and that the event id has changed —
  proving NIP-33 replacement, not just local DB tracking.

* fix(key_packages): propagate canonical tracking failures

Per CodeRabbit review on PR #835: the canonical (kind:30443) tracking
write was being silently swallowed with a tracing::warn!, but the
d-tag reuse and monotonic-created_at invariants both read from this
row on the next publish. If a canonical publish lands but tracking
fails, the next publish thinks no slot exists and starts a fresh
random d-tag — the exact bug this PR fixes.

Split track_published into two helpers in both publish paths:
- track_published_canonical: returns Result, propagated via `?`.
- track_published_legacy: stays best-effort with warn-and-continue,
  since kind:443 is regular per NIP-01 (not addressable) and only
  affects audit-trail completeness, not future canonical replacement.

The accompanying CodeRabbit suggestion to soft-fail the d-tag /
max-created_at lookups is rejected: it explicitly contradicts the
earlier review on this same PR ("Fail the publish when loading the
canonical d tag fails. Falling back to a fresh MDK-generated d here
breaks the exact invariant this PR is adding"). Keeping the `?`
preserves the invariant — DB read failures on the per-account file
are rare, and the scheduler retries on its next tick.

* deps(mdk): bump to 65d02043 and switch to KeyPackageOptions.existing_d_tag

MDK now exposes `KeyPackageOptions { protected, existing_d_tag }` and
`create_key_package_for_event_with_options`. Hand the persisted d-tag
to MDK at key-package-creation time so the returned `tags_30443` and
`KeyPackageEventData::d_tag` are already authoritative — no post-edit
tag rewriting needed.

- Both publish paths (`Whitenoise::publish_key_package_pair_to_relays`
  and `KeyPackageOps::publish_pair`) now consume those inputs directly
  via a new `prepare_canonical_publish_inputs` helper that does the
  slot lookups, generates the key package with the stored d-tag, and
  computes the monotonic canonical `created_at`. The publish functions
  trust the resulting `KeyPackageEventData` and just publish + track.
- Drops the `apply_d_tag_override` helper and its three unit tests:
  the post-edit workaround for MDK's old no-option API is no longer
  needed. The DB tests and the monotonic-timestamp tests stay.
- Test helpers and the maintenance fixture's outdated-key-package
  publisher pass `None` for the new `existing_d_tag` parameter — they
  build one-off KPs that should not slot into the persisted lifecycle.

* fix(key_packages): serialize concurrent rotations per account

Per CodeRabbit review on PR #835: the read-d_tag → read-max →
encode → publish → track sequence is racy. Two concurrent triggers on
the same account (e.g. scheduler tick coinciding with a giftwrap
arrival) could both read the same `find_latest_d_tag` /
`find_max_created_at` values, generate two different MLS key packages
sharing the same `d` tag and the same `canonical_created_at`, and let
the relay's NIP-01 lowest-event-id tiebreaker pick the winner —
defeating the d-tag-reuse + monotonic-timestamp invariants this PR
establishes, and orphaning the loser's local MLS key material.

Add `AccountSession::key_package_publish_lock: Mutex<()>` and acquire
it for the full prepare→publish→track sequence in the three paths
where concurrent triggers are plausible:

- `KeyPackageOps::publish` (scheduler maintenance, giftwrap-consumed
  republish).
- `KeyPackageOps::create_and_publish` (test seeding via the session
  view).
- `Whitenoise::publish_key_package_for_account_with_signer` (external
  signer login).

`create_key_package_and_background_publish` is intentionally left
unlocked: it runs during fresh-account creation, before any other
trigger can fire for the same account, and locking through its
production tokio::spawn would force MLS key material generation off
the synchronous account-creation path that callers rely on.

Also add the empty-relays early return to
`KeyPackageOps::create_and_publish` so it matches `publish()` and
doesn't generate orphan MLS key material when there's nowhere to
publish it.

* fix(key_packages): address review feedback on PR #835

Four follow-ups from jgmontoya:

- **Single DB query for canonical-slot state.** Replace
  `find_latest_d_tag` + `find_max_created_at` with a single
  `find_latest_by_kind` that returns the most recent row. The d-tag and
  the insert timestamp come from the *same* prior publish — splitting
  the lookup into two queries implied they could disagree. Saves a DB
  roundtrip and makes the call site cleaner.

- **Simplify `monotonic_canonical_created_at`.** Use
  `floor.max(now.as_secs())` instead of a branched `if/else`, and rely
  on the `prev >= 0` guard to make `prev as u64` value-preserving.
  Semantically identical, two fewer lines.

- **Race in `create_key_package_and_background_publish`.** My prior
  justification ("nothing else can fire during account creation") was
  wrong: `setup_subscriptions` runs before `setup_key_package`, so the
  giftwrap handler is live by the time the spawn starts. A welcome
  arriving in the race window would let `KeyPackageOps::publish` read
  the same empty state, MDK would generate a different d-tag, and both
  publishes would land in different NIP-33 slots — the very bug this
  PR is fixing. Move the `lock → prepare → publish → track` sequence
  inside the spawn (and the inline-await fallback) so the per-account
  publish lock covers the full atomic unit. Pulls MLS key generation
  into the spawn in production, but no caller relies on local key
  material existing immediately after this function returns.

- **Doc clarity on row vs. event `created_at`.** Update the rustdoc on
  `find_latest_by_kind` and `monotonic_canonical_created_at` to spell
  out that `published_key_packages.created_at` is the SQLite
  `unixepoch()` row-insert timestamp (not the Nostr event's
  `created_at`), and why that still gives a sound monotonic-floor
  guarantee: the INSERT runs after the relay round-trip, so
  `row.created_at ≥ event.created_at` always.

* docs(key_packages): explain why Whitenoise + session publish paths coexist

Per PR #835 review thread on `publish_key_package_pair_to_relays`: the
external-signer login flow inserts the signer into
`Whitenoise.shared.external_signers` *before* `AccountSession::from_account`
runs. `from_account` only loads a session signer for accounts with a
local key, so external accounts get `session.signer = None`. Routing the
initial external-signer publish through `KeyPackageOps::publish_pair`
would then trip `require_signer() → SignerUnavailable`.

Folding the two publish paths into one means rewiring `from_account` (or
`insert_account_session`) to also consult the `external_signers` map —
a session-signer-lifecycle refactor that's out of scope for the
d-tag-stability fix. Document the constraint on the Whitenoise side of
the path so the next reader doesn't have to rediscover it.

* docs(key_packages): trim refactor-history prose from find_latest_by_kind

Per jgmontoya review on PR #835: drop the "Folding both lookups into
one query..." meta-commentary from both the repo wrapper and the
underlying query method. It described the refactor rather than the
behavior and would rot. The behavioral docs on the underlying
`PublishedKeyPackage::find_latest_by_kind` (what d_tag/created_at are
for, the row-insert vs event-time caveat) stay; the thin
`PublishedKeyPackagesRepo` wrapper now matches its sibling one-liner
doc style.

---------
